Method of Attack: Distributed via phishing campaigns using PDF attachments that download Windows Script Files (WSF) to infect Windows devices
Reply-chain phishing emails using stolen email exchanges with malicious attachments or links
WSF files execute obfuscated PowerShell scripts to download DLLs from multiple URLs
Malware injects into legitimate Windows wermgr.exe process to run stealthily
Provides initial access to corporate networks for other threat actors by dropping additional payloads like Cobalt Strike, Brute Ratel, and other malware
Spreads laterally through networks, steals data, and enables ransomware deployment in extortion attacks
Attack Vector: Malicious WSF files executed on Windows
Indicators of Compromise: PDF file named 'CancelationLetter-[number].pdf' containing malicious WSF download
WSF files with obfuscated scripts executing PowerShell to download DLLs
URLs used to download DLLs (multiple URLs tried sequentially)
